newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-REAMS OF VERSE GIVES CECIL FIFTH OAKS TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-REAMS OF VERSE GIVES CECIL FIFTH OAKS TRIUMPH.

text.p: Hot favourite Reams of Verse silenced the critics who said she might not stay to battle her way to victory in the Epsom Oaks on Friday.
Ridden by Irishman Kieren Fallon for top trainer Henry Cecil, she came home one-and-a-half lengths clear of 33-1 French raider Gazelle Royale, the mount of Jimmy Fortune.
Third place, a further threequarters of a length away, went to 11-1 chance Crown of Light, partnered by Frenchman Olivier Peslier.

Reams of Verse, the 5-6 favourite, gave the elegant Cecil his fifth Epsom Oaks success, but owner Prince Khalid Abdullah was winning the fillies' classic for the first time after 10 previous failures dating back to 1987.

The race was a personal triumph for Fallon, newly appointed this season to the top job at Cecil's Newmarket stable. It was his second Classic success of the year following the impressive victory in the Newmarket 1,000 Guineas of Sleepytime.
Ironically, Fallon might have missed the entire Epsom meeting, including his mount in Saturday's Derby, after picking up a recent 10-day ban in Italy.
Happily for the soft-spoken Irishman, the Italian authorities later altered the date of the ban.
Fallon was at his most forceful on Reams of Verse, who some felt might have difficulty on staying the 12 furlongs (2.4 kms) of the race.
The filly, a failure in the 1,000 Guineas but an impressive winner at York last month, drew level with Gazelle Royale in the final 100 metres and ran on gamely to land the $310,000 spoils.
Fallon, coming to grips with the tricky Epsom switchback, said: "She handled the track perfectly. The race went well but we had some traffic problems on the turn.
"If I didn't find trouble, I would have probably kicked sooner than I wanted to. So it turned out well."
Cecil, a master trainer of fillies, said: "She's got class. I am very lucky to have her. I think she probably will take on the colts later on in her career."

The early pace was set by Frankie Dettori on Siyadah with Ukraine Venture, the mount of Willie Ryan, in close attendance and Reams of Verse and Yashmak, also in the Prince Khalid colours, in mid-division in the 12-strong field.
Turning into the 500-metre straight, Ukraine Venture led the way only to be pressed by the Aga Khan's Ebadiyla, seeking revenge for the controversial 1989 disqualification of his Aliysa.
Halfway up the straight, Ebadiyla struck the front, only to be swallowed up by Gazelle Royale setting sail for home in an attempt to defy her 33-1 odds.
Fortune, whose mount veered left, was later given a two-day ban for careless riding but still said: "She is really gutsy. I would love to ride her again."
But Reams of Verse was produced on the scene at exactly the right time by Fallon who always held the upperhand in the closing stages.
